question: Which body area represents the thermal core?

options.A: Skin surface and subcutaneous fat layers
options.B: Deep internal organs of the trunk and head
options.C: Peripheral tissues of the hands and feet
options.D: Superstantial skeletal muscles of the limbs

explanation: The core consists of the central visceral structures inside the cranial, thoracic, and abdominal cavities where vital chemical reactions occur. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why does the temperature of the body shell fluctuate much more than the core?

options.A: It lacks any blood supply to bring warmth from internal organs
options.B: It is directly exposed to changing environmental conditions
options.C: It contains higher concentrations of active brown adipose tissue
options.D: It generates massive amounts of heat during normal resting states

explanation: The skin and peripheral limbs interact directly with outside air and surfaces, causing their temperatures to rise and fall with the weather. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h1)

question: What condition must exist for the body to maintain thermal balance?

options.A: Ambient temperature must equal body temperature
options.B: Metabolic rate must drop to zero
options.C: Skin temperature must match core temperature
options.D: Heat production must equal heat loss

explanation: Thermal balance is achieved only when the amount of heat generated internally matches the amount dissipated into the environment. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why are newborn infants particularly vulnerable to disruptions in thermal balance?

options.A: Their core temperature naturally remains much higher than adults
options.B: Their thick shell prevents any internal heat from escaping
options.C: Their sweat glands overproduce moisture in normal rooms
options.D: Their immature regulatory systems struggle with environmental shifts

explanation: Neonates have high surface-area-to-mass ratios and underdeveloped control mechanisms, making them prone to rapid heat loss. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which part of the central nervous system acts as the primary thermostat for the body?
explanation: The hypothalamus contains specialized neurons that monitor blood temperature and coordinate appropriate physiological responses. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary role of peripheral thermoreceptors?

options.A: Detecting temperature changes in the skin and external environment
options.B: Releasing sweat from eccrine glands during high fevers
options.C: Generating chemical heat through brown fat oxidation
options.D: Directly adjusting the metabolic rate inside the liver and muscles

explanation: Peripheral thermoreceptors monitor surface and environmental thermal conditions and send this sensory input up to the brain. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary source of internal heat production?

options.B: Skeletal muscle movement during physical activity
options.C: Basal metabolism of internal visceral organs
options.D: Direct absorption of sunlight through the skin

explanation: Internal body heat is generated through metabolic processes and muscle activity, not by absorbing sunlight like a cold-blooded animal. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does shivering help raise core body temperature?

options.A: Friction between skin folds generates static thermal energy
options.B: It forces blood away from the skin to trap warmth internally
options.C: It stimulates the thyroid gland to release more thyroxine instantly
options.D: Rapid muscle contractions increase cellular work and heat output

explanation: Shivering involves quick, involuntary contractions of skeletal muscles, converting chemical energy into thermal energy to warm the body. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which heat loss mechanism involves infrared waves moving without physical contact?
explanation: Radiation transfers thermal energy through space via electromagnetic waves from warmer objects to cooler surrounding surfaces. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why does a newborn baby lose heat rapidly when placed directly onto a cold scale?

options.A: Air currents sweep away warm air through active convection
options.B: Moisture on the skin turns into gas through evaporation
options.C: Infrared waves radiate away from the skin via radiation
options.D: Heat transfers directly through physical touch via conduction

explanation: Conduction occurs when two objects touch each other directly, allowing heat to flow from the warmer skin to the colder surface. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h5)

question: What happens to skin blood vessels when the body needs to lose excess heat?

options.D: They harden to trap warm blood

explanation: Vasodilation widens surface blood vessels, bringing warm core blood closer to the skin so heat can escape into the environment. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why does peripheral vasoconstriction occur when a person enters a cold room?

options.A: To increase the amount of heat lost through thermal radiation
options.B: To reduce blood flow to the skin and minimize core heat loss
options.C: To force sweat glands to release moisture for rapid cooling
options.D: To speed up the metabolic rate inside peripheral tissues

explanation: Constricting skin blood vessels acts like insulation, keeping warm blood centered around vital internal organs. [learn more](BMP112_U4_T5#BMP112_U4_T5_h6)
